text: Implement safe asynchronous lifecycle ownership for the native openvela Korvo factory candidate. User wants the complete official factory demo on openvela; do not reduce scope. Write ONLY in your private directory /mnt/d/WSL/esp32s31-delivery/factory-demo-port-e403/lifecycle-review. No full builds, hardware, other workers, or maintained edits. Read current candidate UI at backups/factory-demo-port/ui-port/candidate/openvela-dev/frameworks/runtimes/services/xmsdemo/factory and backend at peripherals-port/candidate. Root integrates them separately. Current Activity::onDestroy calls shutdown synchronously, but native MEDIA calls may take seconds. Need concrete privately modified FactoryActivity/Application/Backend header as necessary and owned managed lifecycle executor, with no detached orphan, no UAF, no backend refs to UI, no unbounded retired backends. FLAT SYSTEM_SERVER_LITE means application lifecycle runs on shared system UI loop, including Application::onDestroy. Cannot move blocking join there. Consider process-lifetime managed joinable executor that retains one retiring backend; fail/retry new backend until previous fully shut down; static/process owner joins at actual process teardown, not Activity/Application onDestroy. Queue capacity guaranteed for ownership transfer, allocation/thread failure path must not strand live backend or block shared loop. All frame leases released by tick; canvas is UI-owned separate storage. Backend factory creation currently unique_ptr and NativeBackend destructor calls shutdown. Avoid fake 500 ms guarantee. Do meaningful host test for ownership across delayed shutdown/reopen and target compile checks using existing compile command DB. Do not call static destructors per app in Lite. Existing constraints in contracts.md. Deliver concrete candidate and result.md promptly, root handles full build. Root will integrate providers and MEDIA capture graph now; don't modify those. English code/docs.
I’ll inspect the candidate UI/backend and lifecycle contract first, then implement the managed executor and run focused host/compile checks entirely in the private review directory.

The UI currently destroys its backend on the shared loop, and the backend destructor repeats `shutdown()`. I’ll put creation, startup, shutdown, and deletion under one process-owned joinable worker. The Activity will hold a move-only lease; closing it will post retirement into a reserved slot, and reopening will retry until that backend is fully destroyed.

The slot will be reserved before backend creation, so retirement needs no allocation and cannot fail because a queue is full. Startup failures will also be cleaned up on the worker. There will be at most one backend, and the design will make no fixed claim about MEDIA shutdown time.

The candidate now releases its reservation on pause and destroy, with no backend deletion or join on those paths. Resume retries acquisition, so delayed retirement prevents overlapping device owners. Frame leases still end within the camera tick, and the LVGL canvas keeps its separate UI-owned buffer. I’m testing blocked shutdown and destructor paths, plus startup and allocation failures.

The first target object checks passed for the executor and Activity. The host test holds shutdown for over 800 ms, verifies that reopen remains busy during both shutdown and destruction, and checks that copied canvas pixels survive backend deletion. It also tests a real static-destructor exit to verify the process owner joins the worker.

The plain host tests passed, including failure recovery and process teardown. I also separated “startup pending” from backend error codes so a real `-EAGAIN` cannot leave the reservation stuck. LeakSanitizer cannot run under this environment’s tracing; I’m rerunning with AddressSanitizer and UBSan enabled and recording that limitation.

I’m adjusting pause handling to preserve the existing RAM recording across pause/resume. Pause and resume will post the latest active state to a fixed slot on the worker, which retries rejected state changes. Destroy will release the backend reservation for retirement.

The updated host suite passes in plain and ASan/UBSan runs, including pause retry and preservation of the same backend session. I’m now checking the final sources with the target compiler and preparing the integration overlay and `result.md`. The full UI and peripheral feature scope remains intact.

The active-state slot now acknowledges completion, and the UI waits for that acknowledgement before submitting commands after resume. This prevents a delayed pause from cancelling a newly submitted command. The contract documents that ordering, the single-backend limit, and the process-only join point.

NuttX’s source shows that process-exit handler registration can fail when its fixed table is full. I’m making that registration explicit and checked before starting the executor, so failure leaves no worker or backend without a teardown handler. Per-Application destruction will still do no join or finalization.

The host tests pass with the exit-registration failure case included, and the seven-file patch passes a dry run against the original candidate. The final reference target objects and relocatable link also passed. The remaining FLAT/Lite checks are running; receipts and the review write-up are in the private directory.

Implemented the private [candidate overlay](</mnt/d/WSL/esp32s31-delivery/factory-demo-port-e403/lifecycle-review/candidate.diff>) and [result.md](</mnt/d/WSL/esp32s31-delivery/factory-demo-port-e403/lifecycle-review/result.md>): managed process ownership, asynchronous retirement, bounded backend count, and preserved pause/resume sessions.

Passed host ownership tests, ASan/UBSan, six target compilations, and two relocatable links. Full demo scope retained; no maintained edits, full builds, or hardware operations.

I mistakenly started and immediately stopped a read-only inspector; no delegated work was used.
